title: I made a browser racing game where 22 cats race robot vacuums
author: ledniv
selftext:
This is Formula Cat. You play as Mochi, a ginger tabby racing a robot vacuum against 21 other cats on 31 circuits inspired by real tracks. Names include Monacat, Meownza, Laguna Purrca, and the full 20.832 km Nürpurrgring Nordschleife.

There’s practice, qualifying, adjustable gearing, and battery-swap pit stops. You share a pit box with your teammate, so arriving while they’re using it means waiting for another cat to finish servicing their vacuum. Your ears flap and your scarf streams behind you as you pick up speed.

I built it with Astra in Codex, starting with a request for an animated cat riding a Roomba that I could see on localhost. From there, I kept iterating and giving specific feedback: the tail looked like it was vibrating, the opponents were too slow, and the handling needed proper braking for corners. Astra helped investigate those problems, implement changes, and run tests and lap-time comparisons. I also asked it to use my [data-oriented-design skill](https://github.com/Data-Oriented-Design-for-Games/data-oriented-design) to guide the architecture as the game grew.

For those interested in the technical side, it’s JavaScript and Three.js, using data-oriented design with preallocated typed arrays and a fixed 120 Hz simulation. The opponents use the same driving physics as the player, including braking, grip, and collisions. Racing lines are optimized offline for lap time and then tested in the actual game with a full grid.

It’s still in development, and I’d love feedback on the handling and racing against the other cats.

Play it here: [formulacat.nitzan.games](https://formulacat.nitzan.games/)
